metadata.title: Curvilinear Geometry, Primary Structure, and a Gröbner Degeneration of Conductor Fiber Cones in a Huneke–Wiegand Family
metadata.description:
For every integer p>=4, a previously constructed symmetric numerical semigroup ring R_p and rigid two-generated monomial ideal determine a conductor ideal T_p whose special fiber C_p = F(T_p) is one-dimensional Cohen-Macaulay, generated in degree one by 10p monomials, with multiplicity 24p. Taking the imported offset bases as input, we prove that C_p ≅ k[xy^a : a ∈ G_p] ⊆ k[x,y]/(y^24p), that its defining ideal J_p is primary to the ideal of positive offsets, with nilpotency index 24p, and that Proj(C_p) is a saturated length-24p curvilinear fat point, locally Gorenstein although the coordinate ring has Cohen-Macaulay type 10p+1. The Kähler differentials split by characteristic.

We then determine the reduced Gröbner basis for graded reverse lexicographic order with X_0 last. Its degree profile is (50p^2-17p, 5p-1, p-2) and no minimal leading monomial contains X_0, which gives a flat Cohen-Macaulay monomial degeneration. The quadratic part, the stabilization of the staircase and the absence of elements in degree five and higher are derived. The classification of the cubic and quartic part, for all p, rests on 16 Presburger obligations decided unsatisfiable by two solvers (Z3 and cvc5) on identical queries; it is machine-verified and not derived. Exact sweeps at every p=4,...,300, an independent clique recomputation and negative controls validate the formulas. We place the results beside the known graded Betti entries of C_p and the characteristic dependence found there.

The results concern the conductor fiber cones of this explicit family; they do not assert that arbitrary monomial fiber cones are primary, curvilinear, Cohen-Macaulay or locally Gorenstein.

Source code, compact artifacts, premise hashes and proofs: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH .
metadata.version_notes: Revision of the evidence classes and the computations. Every result now carries a mark (derived, machine-verified, or derived conditional on machine-verified input); the cubic and quartic classification is stated as machine-verified, not derived. The sixteen Presburger obligations are printed as formulas and were decided by a second solver (cvc5 1.4.2) on queries identical to those certified with Z3 4.16.0. The imported input is stated with exact theorem pointers and the sumset identity. The degree-five-and-later argument covers monomials of offset at least q. New sections: related work, algorithms with pseudocode and costs, experimental design, results tables with full hashes, ablation, discussion of the graded Betti entries and their characteristic dependence, limitations. The title is singular (one degeneration). The Huneke-Wiegand reference carries its correct DOI.
